newsitem.title: FINLAND: Imatran Voima sees 1996 profit up 45 pct.
newsitem.headline: Imatran Voima sees 1996 profit up 45 pct.

text.p: Finnish state-controlled energy group Imatran Voima Oy (IVO) said in a statement on Friday it expected full-year 1996 profit before extraordinary items and tax to rise to 1.6 billion markka from 1.1 billion in 1995.
IVO is a leading candidate for privatisation in 1997.
It said full-year net sales would rise to over 12 billion markka from eight billion. Most of the rise in sales came from abroad, largely as a result of acquisitions, it said.
Due to the acquisitions, IVO's balance sheet swelled to about 29 billion markka from 16 billion.
Return on investment would remain unchanged around 12 percent while return on equity would rise to over 12 percent from nine percent last year, the company said.
In the statement, IVO CEO Kalevi Numminen, who retires at end-March, called the forecast 1996 operating result good.
